function.name: check_smiles_reaction_template_matching

function.name: search_template_catalog_by_criteria
function.description: Searches the retrosynthetic template database based on specified criteria. The search criteria refer to the forward reaction.

molecule_smiles.description: SMILES string of the target molecule.
molecule_smiles.title: Molecule Smiles

functional_groups_broken.description: List of functional groups that are broken in the forward reaction. None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
functional_groups_broken.title: Functional Groups Broken

functional_groups_formed.description: List of functional groups that are formed in the forward reaction. None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
functional_groups_formed.title: Functional Groups Formed

bonds_formed.description: List of bonds that are formed in the forward reaction (e.g., "6-6", "6-8"). None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
bonds_formed.title: Bonds Formed

bonds_broken.description: List of bonds that are broken in the forward reaction (e.g., "6-6", "6-8"). None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
bonds_broken.title: Bonds Broken

bonds_order_changed.description: List of bonds whose order is changed in the forward reaction (e.g., "6-6 (1.0->2.0)"). None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
bonds_order_changed.title: Bonds Order Changed

limit.description: Maximum number of templates to return. Default is 10.
limit.title: Limit

Let me understand the task:
1. I need to propose a retrosynthesis route for the molecule: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O
2. The route must have exactly 6 reactions
3. I'm given hints for the forward reactions in order, so I need to reverse them for retrosynthesis

Let me parse the target molecule SMILES first to understand its structure:
O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

This appears to be a complex molecule with:
- A sulfonamide group (S(=O)2-NH-)
- A fluorophenyl group attached to the sulfur
- An aromatic ring with a piperazine substituent (with Boc protection)
- A cyclic ether structure

The 6 reactions in forward direction are:
1. Sulfonamide formation: aromatic amine + phenylsulfonyl chloride → sulfonamide
2. Nitro reduction: nitro group → amine
3. SNAr: nucleophile replaces halogen on aromatic ring
4. Electrophilic bromination: H on aromatic ring → Br
5. Wolff-Kishner reduction: ketone → alkane
6. Cyclization of chalcones to flavanones: chalcone → flavanone (intramolecular Michael addition)

Since I need to do retrosynthesis, I need to reverse these:
- Step 6 (last forward) becomes Step 1 (first retro): flavanone → chalcone
- Step 5 becomes Step 2: alkane → ketone
- Step 4 becomes Step 3: Br on aromatic → H on aromatic
- Step 3 becomes Step 4: C-N bond → C-halogen bond
- Step 2 becomes Step 5: amine → nitro
- Step 1 becomes Step 6: sulfonamide → amine + sulfonyl chloride

Working backwards from the target, the cyclic ether structure suggests the first retrosynthetic step should break open the flavanone ring to reveal the underlying chalcone precursor with a ketone group and an unsaturated side chain.

The ketone then traces back to a saturated alkane via Wolff-Kishner reduction. Bromine substituents on the aromatic ring need to be replaced with hydrogens. The C-N bond connecting the amine to the aromatic system came from an SNAr displacement of a halogen. The amine itself originated from reduction of a nitro group. Finally, the sulfonamide linkage formed from coupling an amine with a sulfonyl chloride reagent.

I need to search the template database for transformations matching these steps and identify the functional groups present in the target molecule to work through the synthesis systematically.
